issues.failure_explanation: Operator-norm convergence gives no such convergence of nonclosed operator ranges. The claimed identity is false even without sign cancellation: take D=(0,1)^3, S(y)=y_1^2, c=1, direction e_1, t_0=2, κ=1/2 and K=1/4. Both real and imaginary parts of the multiplier are positive, so F#=LML*, where M(y) is bounded above and below by positive constants times y_1^2. Thus Range(F#^{1/2})=Range(LM^{1/2}). But L1 is not in this range: equality would force the cross-sectional average of a preimage to behave as 1/y_1, which is not square-integrable. All stated source assumptions hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the uniform nonvanishing bound used for the earlier range identity and remove the limiting argument. Retaining the advertised nodal-set class instead requires an appropriate weighted-space range theorem and corresponding reconstruction analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The unweighted range identity and the resulting Picard criteria are not established for sources that merely satisfy almost-everywhere nonvanishing.
issues.title: Norm convergence does not preserve the exact ranges used in the relaxed range identity
issues.why_classification: The direct repair abandons the explicitly advertised relaxation allowing zeros. Preserving that source class requires a different functional setting and new range-based analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: Every finite-dimensional range contains e^{-iτa_1}, but no pure exponential e^{-iτb} belongs to Range(L). Indeed, an L2(D) density is integrable on bounded D, and its projection onto the observation coordinate has an L1 density. Its Fourier transform tends to zero at large real frequencies. Equality with a pure exponential on (0,K) would extend to all frequencies by analyticity, contradicting this decay. Thus neither the intended increasing-range limit nor the inference used in Theorem lem3.4 is valid. This failure persists for uniformly positive sources.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace the point exponentials by realizable L2-source test patterns, or change the source spaces and range criterion, and reprove the indicator and reconstruction results.
issues.overall_effect: The central point-test characterization is false: its proposed test functions are outside the volume-source range even for points strictly inside the strip. The asserted positive indicator regions consequently have no valid foundation.
issues.title: Finite-dimensional exponential ranges do not converge to the volume-source range
issues.why_classification: The advertised rigorous justification of pointwise exponential tests cannot survive as stated. Repair requires a different test construction or functional framework and a replacement reconstruction argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A discrete approximation of the far-field operator ${F}^{(\hat x)}$ is given  by the Toeplitz matrix

issues.failure_explanation: This eigenvector reuse and eigenvalue mapping is not valid for general nonnormal matrices. The Toeplitz discretization is not guaranteed to be normal, even at κ=0 because its input and output grids are staggered. For example, a real matrix A=[[a,a],[b,a]] with 0<b<a has eigenvalues a±sqrt(ab), whereas |Re A|+|Im A| has eigenvalues 2a and a-b, using the Hermitian operator parts. Staggered samples of a constant positive box profile can have this form.

failure_location.quote: then one deduces that  an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$ is $\left\{ ( \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n, \psi^{(\hat x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$, where $ \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n:=|\real (\tilde \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n)| +|\ima (\tilde \lambda^{( \hat x)}_n)|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Form H=(F+F*)/2 and G=(F-F*)/(2i), compute their operator absolute values, and diagonalize |H|+|G| directly rather than transforming the eigensystem of F.
issues.overall_effect: The prescribed shortcut can supply incorrect eigenvectors and spectral weights to every numerical indicator.
issues.title: The numerical eigensystem transformation is invalid for nonnormal far-field matrices
issues.why_classification: Direct diagonalization of the actual positive matrix is a routine local replacement, already compatible with the alternative numerical approach mentioned in the source.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses omit a condition preventing cancellation under compression by L. Take X=C^2, Y=C, L(z_1,z_2)=z_1+z_2 and T=diag(1+i,-1-i). All stated hypotheses hold, including T#=2I, but F=LTL*=0 while Range(L)=C. The same obstruction occurs in the paper's source class: for D a ball, S(y)=y_2 and direction e_1, both opposite-direction far fields vanish identically for every excitation time. Thus almost-everywhere nonvanishing does not imply the claimed two-direction uniqueness.

failure_location.quote: Then the operator $F_{\#}$ is positive and  the ranges of $F_{\#}^{1/2}:Y\rightarrow Y$ and  $L: X\rightarrow Y$ coincide.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated operator hypothesis by suitable fixed-sign conditions on the real and imaginary parts together with coercivity, so that F#=L T# L* is justified, and impose the corresponding source-sign and phase restrictions in the applications. The unrestricted signed-source and arbitrary-phase claims must otherwise be withdrawn or proved by a different method.
issues.overall_effect: The supporting range theorem is false, its applications do not justify the range identities, and the two-direction uniqueness assertion is actually false for allowed sign-changing sources.
issues.title: The abstract range theorem permits cancellation and is false
issues.why_classification: A valid restricted theorem excludes source and frequency-phase regimes covered by the paper, and the unrestricted two-direction uniqueness cannot be preserved because of explicit indistinguishable sources.
